Emma Watson overlaid on Kasey Chase. Full render of the same clip I used in the 20 second test vid. A lot of spots didn't turn out, so I combined the segments that were good or not too bad.

Layers: 1024, nodes: 8, batch: 256, seamless: false, blur: 10, kernel: 8, hardware: 1080 ti, training time: a few days, loss at combine time: ~0.012, data_B images: ~12k.

What I learned:

  • Facial obstructions are difficult! Tried to do some of a blowjob scene but it just didn't turn out. It was also too close. Per some other posts, I'm going to try A-to-A self-training prior to A-to-B training on a new vid to see if it works.

  • Close up images need a different blend method. Would make sense to combine these in a different batch. As you can see in some of the closer shots, the face box is visible, whereas it is not visible on the far away shots. Increasing the blur and kernel to 15 or higher would probably have helped.

  • I don't think a pretrained model is as important as a decent image set + a lot of time. Getting the loss value low seems to help a lot.

  • You are at the mercy of the face extraction tool. There are scenes where it just didn't detect a face. Unless someone writes a program where you can manually define face boxes on frames and it adds it to the alignments.json, creating a good video will mean getting full or partial face in there. The more unusual angles just don't extract properly.
